To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dietary intake of glucose and fructose increases hepatic triacylglycerole synthesis by accelerating the conversion of diacylglycerols to triacylglycerols, and that this effect is due to an increase in the activity of the enzyme phosphatidate phosphaohydrolase.
the diets containing glucose and fructose increased the activity of two enzymes that catalyzed the formation of endogenous triaclyglycerol from glycerol-3P, ATP, palmtate and CoA.
dietary fructose or glucose increased the formation of triacyglcerol by various liver cell preparations in the presence of glycerol-3-phosphate, ATP, palmtiate, and coenzyme A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary fructose and glucose on the synthesis of hepatic lipids.
the effect of dietary carbohydrates, especially glucose and fructose, on hepatic lipid metabolism and on the regulation of the enzymes involved in the formation of endogenous lipid.
the effects of dietary fructose on hepatic glyceride metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diets high in glucose or fructose increase the activity of the enzyme phosphatidate-phosphohydrolase which in turn increases the rate of triacylglyerol formation by liver.
the increased formation of triaacylglycerol is due to increased activity of phosphatidate-phosphohydrolase.
dietary glucose and fructose cause a marked and rapid increase in hepatic microsomal phosphatidate-phosphohydrolase (PAP) activity, which in turn leads to increased triacylgycerol synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary induced changes in hepatic triacylglyceride metabolism are due to changes in the activity of phosphatidate-phosphohydrolase.
dietary fructose or glucose induces an increase in hepatic phosphatidate and triacylglycerols.

the increased activity of the microsomal phosphatidate-phosphohydrolase and the supernatant fraction of phosphatidate- phosphohydrolases, which is probably cytosolic in nature, are responsible for the increased rate of triacylglyerol synthesis by liver cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dietary sugar is the primary factor in determining the amount of triacylgycerol synthesized by the liver.

dietary sugars can cause an increase in hepatic triacylglyceride formation and that the mechanism for the increase in triacyglyceride formation is an increased activity of the enzyme phosphatidatephosphohydrolase.

the high fructose diet increases the activity of two enzymes in the liver, sn-glycer-3-P acylation and phosphatidic acid phosphohydrolases, and that the increase in these activities results in an increased rate of triacylglyerol formation by the liver.
